title: The 45-Minute Interview Roadmap
summary: Pace a system design interview cleanly from scoping to deep dives without running out of time.
body:
Strong candidates treat a 45-minute design interview as a linear progression that delivers a working end-to-end system first, then spends remaining time proving technical depth on the hardest bottlenecks.

## 1. Requirements and scope (~5 min)
Pin down the top 3 to 4 user-facing capabilities and quantify the system qualities that actually shape the architecture.
- Functional: state concrete actions (`upload 50 GB file`, `book assigned seat`, `query top K over 1 hour`) and explicitly call out non-goals.
- Non-functional: quantify latency targets, read-to-write skew, traffic spikes, and where consistency beats availability (for example checkout vs search).

## 2. Core entities (~2 min)
List the 3 to 5 nouns your APIs exchange and your storage layer persists before drawing boxes.
- Keep it light (`User`, `Event`, `SeatHold`, `Order`), saving full column types and partition keys for the deep dive.

## 3. API and system interface (~5 min)
Write one endpoint or RPC per functional requirement so your diagram has concrete entry points.
- Include auth context, pagination cursors (`cursor` rather than SQL `OFFSET`), and idempotency keys on mutating writes.

## 4. High-level architecture (~13 min)
Trace each API from client to storage until every functional requirement works at moderate scale.
- Group components logically using Excalidraw frames and label arrows with protocols or actions.

## 5. Deep dives and tradeoffs (~20 min)
Proactively pick the 2 or 3 hardest bottlenecks—do not wait passively if you are targeting Senior or Staff+.
- Mid-Level: deliver a clean, complete working design and handle guided follow-up questions.
- Senior: move briskly through basics to spend half the session on scaling bottlenecks, failure modes, and tradeoffs.
- Staff+: frame constraints decisively, avoid over-engineering when a single server suffices, and address blast-radius isolation, multi-region behavior, and operational cost.
